            int documents = args.length > 1 ? Integer.parseInt(args[1]) : 64;
            int annotationsPerDocument = args.length > 2 ? Integer.parseInt(args[2]) : 500;
            System.out.println(DUAStreamingCasEvaluator
                    .evaluateDenseEphemeral(documents, annotationsPerDocument)
                    .summaryLine());
            System.out.println(DUAStreamingCasEvaluator
                    .evaluateSqlitePersistent(documents, annotationsPerDocument)
                    .summaryLine());
            return;
        }
        DUAEvaluationWorkload workload = args.length > 0 && args[0].equalsIgnoreCase("standard")
                ? DUAEvaluationWorkload.standard()
                : DUAEvaluationWorkload.smoke();
        DUAStorageEvaluationReport report = DUACasStorageEvaluator.evaluate(workload, true);
        DUAEvaluationResult baseline = report.baseline();
        System.out.println(report.summary());
        for (DUAEvaluationResult result : report.results()) {
            if (result == baseline) {
                continue;
            }
            double readRatio = result.readOpsPerSecond() / baseline.readOpsPerSecond();
            double writeRatio = result.writeOpsPerSecond() / baseline.writeOpsPerSecond();
            double concurrentRatio = result.concurrentWriteOpsPerSecond() / baseline.concurrentWriteOpsPerSecond();
            System.out.printf("%s ratios vs heap: write=%.3f read=%.3f vt-write=%.3f%n",
                    result.name(), writeRatio, readRatio, concurrentRatio);
        }
    }
}

```

[uce-postgres-query-evaluation.md](/home/stud_homes/s0424382/projects/ttlab/duui-alpha/duui-dua/docs/uce-postgres-query-evaluation.md:1) now evaluates the **best DUA database backend architecture** from the UCE PostgreSQL query workloads.

The decision is explicit:

```text
PostgreSQL typed projection warehouse as primary query backend
+ DUA tiered CAS/KV/object storage as canonical lazy JCas backend
+ shard-local deployment for distribution
+ optional sidecars for text relevance, vectors, analytics
+ graph as navigation projection, not storage authority
```

# DUA Database Backend Architecture From UCE PostgreSQL Query Workloads

This document evaluates the best database backend architecture for complex,
wide-ranging DUA queries over large corpora, using the local UCE PostgreSQL
functions and the BioFID Nova sample as the workload reference.

It is not a UCE migration plan.

## Corpus Evidence

Local sample:

`/home/stud_homes/s0424382/projects/ttlab/uce/biofid-nova-preprocessing/preprocessed_corpora_sample_1000`

| metric | value |
| --- | ---: |
| sample documents | 1000 |
| source corpus documents | 24,035 |
| compressed sample size | 436,604,816 bytes |
| compressed mean document size | 436,604.8 bytes |
| compressed p50 | 388,122 bytes |
| compressed p90 | 613,071 bytes |
| compressed p95 | 769,605 bytes |
| compressed p99 | 1,203,538 bytes |
| compressed max | 2,040,700 bytes |

The 24k BioFID corpus is not "big data" for a relational engine if the data is
physically modeled correctly. It is too large for heap-CAS-wide processing and
too relationally diverse for a pure graph backend, but it is exactly the scale
where PostgreSQL with typed projections, partitions, fulltext, PostGIS, and
materialized views should perform well.

## Workload Extracted From UCE

| UCE source | query workload | backend implication |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `uce_search_layer_fulltext` | fulltext over pages, metadata filters, permissions, ranking, snippets, optional annotation facets | primary engine needs fulltext, typed metadata, joins, and materialized candidate sets |
| metadata filter CTEs | key/value filters plus numeric range casts from string values | metadata must be stored in typed columns, not stringly values |
| `uce_semantic_role_search` | event matching by verb, ARG roles, role aliases, document scope, sorted metadata | SRL is a relational event-table problem, not graph traversal |
| `get_corpus_annotations` | corpus-wide counts over annotation families | needs precomputed doc/corpus summary projections |
| geoname timeline functions | bounding boxes, date ranges, corpus filters, clustering | PostGIS plus materialized views is the right architecture |
| `refresh_links` | dynamic annotation-table id resolution | DUA must resolve typed FS ids at ingest and write canonical edges |
| `permitted_documents` | repeatedly returns full document rows for scope filtering | DUA needs indexed document-id scope sets/ACL projections |
| `AgeGraphService` | AGE used mostly as property tables, with hot predicates extracted from `agtype` | graph DB is useful for navigation mirrors, not primary query storage |
| embedding/topic tables | vector, topic, and distribution lookups joined back to documents | vector search must still join to scope, metadata, and annotation projections |

## Backend Candidates

| backend | verdict | reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UIMA heap CAS | baseline only | Correctness and JCas latency baseline; memory grows with loaded CAS payloads. |
| SQLite CAS store | local durable CAS backend | Good for portable `.dua` shards and tests; not the best primary engine for multi-user wide queries. |
| RocksDB/LMDB/FoundationDB KV | strong CAS point-read backend | Excellent for lazy slot/array reads and write bursts; weak for ad hoc text/metadata/SRL/geospatial queries. |
| PostgreSQL typed projection | primary query backend | Best fit for UCE-shaped workloads: joins, fulltext, metadata, SRL, ACL, PostGIS, pgvector, materialized views. |
| Citus/sharded PostgreSQL | distributed query backend | Natural scale-out path: shard by corpus/document, fan out candidate queries, merge top-k windows. |
| PostgreSQL AGE | optional graph mirror only | UCE shows AGE becomes expensive when hot predicates live inside `agtype` properties. |
| Neo4j/TigerGraph/graph DB | not primary | Useful for graph algorithms, but UIMA feature data and BioFID search are dominated by typed point/range/text queries. |
| OpenSearch/Lucene | optional text sidecar | Useful for fuzzy/prefix/relevance-heavy search; should return page/document ids to PostgreSQL/DUA. |
| DuckDB/Parquet | offline analytical sidecar | Strong for read-only corpus analytics; not ideal for mutable concurrent DUA state. |
| ClickHouse | optional large inspector analytics | Strong for massive aggregate dashboards; overkill for 24k docs unless UI analytics dominate. |
| MongoDB/document store | not primary | Flexible, but weaker for typed joins, permissions, SRL event matching, and geospatial/text/vector in one plan. |

## Recommended DUA Architecture

DUA should use a four-plane architecture.

| plane | backend | purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CAS materialization plane | DUA tiered CAS storage: dense hot memory plus SQLite/KV/object/columnar durable stores | lazy JCas-compatible reads/writes with bounded active memory |
| query projection plane | PostgreSQL typed projection schema | fulltext, metadata, SRL, annotation summaries, geospatial/time, permissions, vectors, topics |
| distributed execution plane | shard-local PostgreSQL or Citus-style distributed PostgreSQL | query fan-out over DUA archive shards, local candidate pruning, global top-k merge |
| navigation/inspector plane | relational adjacency first; optional AGE/RDF/GraphML/OpenSearch/ClickHouse mirrors | graph browsing, visualization, offline analytics, specialized UI components |

The primary database backend for complex BioFID-scale wide queries is:

```text
shard-local PostgreSQL typed projections + DUA tiered CAS storage
```

For a single-machine 24k BioFID deployment:

```text
one PostgreSQL database
+ partitioned typed projection tables
+ DUA archive/CAS storage on local disk/object store
+ optional OpenSearch only if PostgreSQL fulltext relevance is insufficient
```

For distributed corpora:

```text
one DUA universe manifest
+ N corpus/document shards
+ one projection database per shard or Citus hash partitions
+ coordinator sends candidate-set queries to shards
+ coordinator merges compact document/page/FS ids
+ CAS plane materializes only the visible result window
```

## Physical Model

The query projection must be derived from CAS/XMI but not store hot predicates
as generic strings or graph properties.

Required table families:

- `document`: universe id, corpus id, document id, shard id, title term,
  parsed publication date/year, language, snapshot epoch.
- `page`: document id, view id, page id, begin/end, text, generated `tsvector`.
- `metadata`: typed term/i64/f64/bool/date/timestamp/spatial columns.
- `fs`: FS ref, type id, view id, document id, binary GID.
- `annotation_span`: begin/end, type id, covered-term id.
- `feature_*`: type-specific feature indexes for i64/f64/bool/term/ref.
- `srl_event` and `srl_role`: verb term id, role mask, role code, ground term.
- `association_edge`: association kind, type id, source ref/GID, target ref/GID,
  sequence index, weight.
- `annotation_summary`: doc-level and corpus-level mention counts.
- `timeline_event`: materialized PostGIS/date projection.
- `acl/scope`: principal/document permission projections or compressed bitmaps.

The current DUA schema contracts already point in this direction:

- `src/main/resources/dua/schema/postgres/query-backend-v1.sql`
- `src/main/resources/dua/schema/postgres/query-patterns-v1.sql`
- `src/main/resources/dua/schema/sqlite/cas-storage-v1.sql`

## Query Execution Strategy

UCE's current fulltext function does too much in one dynamic CTE stack. DUA
should compile every wide query into candidate-set stages:

1. Scope:
   choose universe, corpus, shard, view, ACL, and snapshot.

2. Independent candidates:
   fulltext pages, metadata filters, SRL role/event hits, annotation terms,
   geospatial/date ranges, association neighborhoods, vector candidates.

3. Candidate algebra:
   intersect/union document ids and FS refs before detail joins.

4. Ranking:
   rank only the candidate set.

5. Lazy detail fetch:
   fetch snippets, labels, facets, and CAS/JCas materialization only for the
   requested result window.

This is the critical difference between a database-backed DUA and a heap CAS
pipeline: broad queries return ids first, and CAS payloads stay cold until the
user or pipeline touches them.

## Why Graph Is Not Primary

The UCE AGE service is the evidence. It imports nodes and associations into AGE,
but the UI queries mostly do:

- filter by corpus id;
- filter by document id;
- filter by UIMA type;
- search names/UIDs;
- count incoming/outgoing edges;
- page/sort results;
- expand shallow ego neighborhoods.

Those are adjacency-table and typed-index workloads. Hiding corpus, document,
type, UID, and name inside `agtype` properties makes the planner's job harder.

DUA should still support graph views, but as generated projections:

```text
typed FS/association tables -> graph mirror/export -> inspector visualization
```

not:

```text
graph DB -> all CAS/query state
```

## Expected Architecture By Scale

| scale | recommended backend |
| --- | --- |
| single document / unit tests | heap CAS and dense memory backend |
| local `.dua` bundle | SQLite CAS store plus optional SQLite/JSONL graph indexes |
| 1000-document BioFID sample | PostgreSQL typed projection plus DUA tiered CAS store |
| 24,035-document BioFID corpus | partitioned PostgreSQL typed projection plus DUA tiered CAS store |
| multi-corpus/multi-user service | shard-local PostgreSQL or Citus, object-store `.dua` shards, gRPC CAS service |
| huge read-only analytics | PostgreSQL for interactive ids, ClickHouse/DuckDB/Parquet sidecar for aggregate dashboards |
| relevance-heavy search | PostgreSQL coordinator plus OpenSearch/Lucene sidecar returning page/document ids |

## Final Decision

The best DUA backend architecture for complex wide-ranging BioFID queries is:

```text
PostgreSQL typed projection warehouse as primary query backend
+ DUA tiered CAS/KV/object storage as canonical lazy JCas backend
+ shard-local deployment for distribution
+ optional sidecars for text relevance, vectors, and analytics
+ graph as navigation projection, not storage authority
```

This architecture satisfies the original DUA goals:

- low memory footprint: only active CAS windows materialize;
- lazy pipelined processing: query plane returns ids, CAS plane loads on demand;
- concurrent access: Postgres handles read concurrency, CAS backend handles
  virtual-thread slot writes and WAL/service persistence;
- corpus/document scope switching: same projection schema has universe, corpus,
  document, view, and FS ids;
- flexible relationships: associations are typed adjacency rows with optional
  graph mirrors;
- practical BioFID performance: UCE's successful PostGIS/materialized-view
  pattern is kept, while string-cast metadata, temp SRL tables, and AGE property
  predicates are removed from hot paths.

```

-- DUA PostgreSQL Query Backend Schema v1
--
-- Purpose:
--   Read-optimized corpus-wide query projections for DUA universes.
--
-- Non-goals:
--   This schema is not the canonical CAS slot/array store. CAS/JCas storage
--   remains identifier-first in the DUA CAS backend. These tables are derived
--   projections for fulltext, metadata, annotation, semantic-role, geospatial,
--   association, and inspector queries.
--
-- Physical rules:
--   * Hot identity is numeric or fixed binary.
--   * Repeated text is dictionary coded through dua_q_term.
--   * Queryable feature values are split by physical type.
--   * Graph/association data uses typed adjacency tables first.
--   * Cold display payloads may use JSONB, but hot predicates must not depend
--     on JSONB/agtype extraction.

CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS btree_gin;
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS postgis;
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dua_q_meta (
    key text PRIMARY KEY,
    value text NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO dua_q_meta(key, value)
VALUES ('schema_name', 'dua-postgres-query-backend'),
       ('schema_version', '1')
ON CONFLICT (key) DO NOTHING;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dua_q_universe (
    universe_id bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    universe_gid bytea NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (octet_length(universe_gid) IN (16, 32)),
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    format_version smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    label_term_id bigint
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dua_q_corpus (
    universe_id bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES dua_q_universe(universe_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    corpus_id bigint NOT NULL,
    corpus_gid bytea NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(corpus_gid) IN (16, 32)),
    external_id_term_id bigint,
    label_term_id bigint,
    document_count bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    PRIMARY KEY (universe_id, corpus_id),
    UNIQUE (universe_id, corpus_gid)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dua_q_term (
    term_id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    value text NOT NULL,
    value_norm text GENERATED ALWAYS AS (lower(value)) STORED,
    value_hash bytea NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(value_hash) IN (8, 16, 32)),
    UNIQUE (value_hash, value)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_dua_q_term_norm_trgm
    ON dua_q_term USING gin (value_norm gin_trgm_ops);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dua_q_type (
    type_id integer GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    uima_type_term_id bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES dua_q_term(term_id),
    super_type_id integer REFERENCES dua_q_type(type_id),
    is_annotation boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    is_array boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    UNIQUE (uima_type_term_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dua_q_feature (
    feature_id integer GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    domain_type_id integer REFERENCES dua_q_type(type_id),
    feature_name_term_id bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES dua_q_term(term_id),
    range_type_id integer REFERENCES dua_q_type(type_id),
    value_kind smallint NOT NULL CHECK (value_kind BETWEEN 1 AND 12),
    UNIQUE (domain_type_id, feature_name_term_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dua_q_view (
    universe_id bigint NOT NULL,
    corpus_id bigint NOT NULL,
    view_id integer NOT NULL,
    view_gid bytea NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(view_gid) IN (16, 32)),
    name_term_id bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES dua_q_term(term_id),
    sofa_id bigint,
    PRIMARY KEY (universe_id, corpus_id, view_id),
    UNIQUE (universe_id, corpus_id, view_gid),
    FOREIGN KEY (universe_id, corpus_id)
        REFERENCES dua_q_corpus(universe_id, corpus_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dua_q_document (
    universe_id bigint NOT NULL,
    corpus_id bigint NOT NULL,
    document_id bigint NOT NULL,
    document_gid bytea NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(document_gid) IN (16, 32)),
    external_id_term_id bigint REFERENCES dua_q_term(term_id),
    title_term_id bigint REFERENCES dua_q_term(term_id),
    author_term_id bigint REFERENCES dua_q_term(term_id),
    language_code smallint,
    published_date date,
    published_year integer,
    ordinal_in_corpus bigint NOT NULL,
    shard_id integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    snapshot_epoch bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    deleted boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    PRIMARY KEY (universe_id, corpus_id, document_id),
    UNIQUE (universe_id, corpus_id, document_gid),
    UNIQUE (universe_id, corpus_id, ordinal_in_corpus),
    FOREIGN KEY (universe_id, corpus_id)
        REFERENCES dua_q_corpus(universe_id, corpus_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_dua_q_document_corpus_date
    ON dua_q_document (universe_id, corpus_id, published_date, document_id)
    WHERE deleted = false;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_dua_q_document_shard
    ON dua_q_document (universe_id, corpus_id, shard_id, document_id)
    WHERE deleted = false;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dua_q_document_acl (
    universe_id bigint NOT NULL,
    corpus_id bigint NOT NULL,
    document_id bigint NOT NULL,
    principal_hash bytea NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(principal_hash) IN (8, 16, 32)),
    permission_level smallint NOT NULL,
    valid_from timestamptz,
    valid_to timestamptz,
    PRIMARY KEY (universe_id, corpus_id, document_id, principal_hash),
    FOREIGN KEY (universe_id, corpus_id, document_id)
        REFERENCES dua_q_document(universe_id, corpus_id, document_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_dua_q_document_acl_principal
    ON dua_q_document_acl (principal_hash, permission_level, universe_id, corpus_id, document_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dua_q_page (
    universe_id bigint NOT NULL,
    corpus_id bigint NOT NULL,
    document_id bigint NOT NULL,
    view_id integer NOT NULL,
    page_id bigint NOT NULL,
    page_gid bytea NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(page_gid) IN (16, 32)),
    begin_i32 integer NOT NULL CHECK (begin_i32 >= 0),

);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_dua_q_page_textsearch

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_dua_q_page_document_order

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dua_q_fs (
    universe_id bigint NOT NULL,

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_dua_q_fs_type

-- DUA PostgreSQL Query Patterns v1
--
-- Purpose:
--   Concrete query entry points over postgres/query-backend-v1.sql. These are
--   candidate-set primitives, not monolithic application procedures.

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dua_q_scope_documents(
    p_universe_id bigint,
    p_corpus_id bigint,
    p_principal_hash bytea DEFAULT NULL,
    p_min_permission_level smallint DEFAULT 1
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    universe_id bigint,
    corpus_id bigint,
    document_id bigint
)
LANGUAGE sql
STABLE
AS $$
    SELECT d.universe_id, d.corpus_id, d.document_id
      FROM dua_q_document d
     WHERE d.universe_id = p_universe_id
       AND d.corpus_id = p_corpus_id
       AND d.deleted = false
       AND (
            p_principal_hash IS NULL
            OR EXISTS (
                SELECT 1
                  FROM dua_q_document_acl acl
                 WHERE acl.universe_id = d.universe_id
                   AND acl.corpus_id = d.corpus_id
                   AND acl.document_id = d.document_id
                   AND acl.principal_hash = p_principal_hash
                   AND acl.permission_level >= COALESCE(p_min_permission_level, 0)
                   AND (acl.valid_from IS NULL OR acl.valid_from <= now())
                   AND (acl.valid_to IS NULL OR acl.valid_to > now())
            )
       );
$$;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dua_q_fulltext_candidates(
    p_universe_id bigint,
    p_corpus_id bigint,
    p_query tsquery,
    p_principal_hash bytea DEFAULT NULL,
    p_min_permission_level smallint DEFAULT 1,
    p_limit integer DEFAULT 1000
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    universe_id bigint,
    corpus_id bigint,
    document_id bigint,
    best_page_id bigint,
    rank_score real
)
LANGUAGE sql
STABLE
AS $$
    WITH scoped AS MATERIALIZED (
        SELECT document_id
          FROM dua_q_scope_documents(
              p_universe_id,
              p_corpus_id,
              p_principal_hash,
              p_min_permission_level
          )
    ),
    page_hits AS MATERIALIZED (
        SELECT p.universe_id,
               p.corpus_id,
               p.document_id,
               p.page_id,
               ts_rank_cd(p.textsearch, p_query) AS rank_score
          FROM dua_q_page p
          JOIN scoped s ON s.document_id = p.document_id
         WHERE p.universe_id = p_universe_id
           AND p.corpus_id = p_corpus_id
           AND p.textsearch @@ p_query
    ),
    ranked AS (
        SELECT DISTINCT ON (document_id)
               universe_id,
               corpus_id,
               document_id,
               page_id AS best_page_id,
               rank_score
          FROM page_hits
         ORDER BY document_id, rank_score DESC, page_id
    )
    SELECT *
      FROM ranked
     ORDER BY rank_score DESC, document_id
     LIMIT COALESCE(p_limit, 1000);
$$;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dua_q_metadata_term_candidates(
    p_universe_id bigint,
    p_corpus_id bigint,
    p_key_id integer,
    p_term_id bigint,
    p_principal_hash bytea DEFAULT NULL,
    p_min_permission_level smallint DEFAULT 1
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    universe_id bigint,
    corpus_id bigint,
    document_id bigint
)
LANGUAGE sql
STABLE
AS $$
    SELECT m.universe_id, m.corpus_id, m.document_id
      FROM dua_q_document_metadata m
      JOIN dua_q_scope_documents(
          p_universe_id,
          p_corpus_id,
          p_principal_hash,
          p_min_permission_level
      ) s ON s.document_id = m.document_id
     WHERE m.universe_id = p_universe_id
       AND m.corpus_id = p_corpus_id
       AND m.key_id = p_key_id
       AND m.term_id = p_term_id;
$$;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dua_q_srl_candidates(
    p_universe_id bigint,
    p_corpus_id bigint,
    p_verb_term_id bigint,
    p_role_codes smallint[],
    p_ground_term_ids bigint[],
    p_principal_hash bytea DEFAULT NULL,
    p_min_permission_level smallint DEFAULT 1,
    p_limit integer DEFAULT 1000
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    universe_id bigint,
    corpus_id bigint,
    document_id bigint,
    view_id integer,
    event_id bigint,
    predicate_begin_i32 integer
)
LANGUAGE sql
STABLE
AS $$
    WITH scoped AS MATERIALIZED (
        SELECT document_id
          FROM dua_q_scope_documents(
              p_universe_id,
              p_corpus_id,
              p_principal_hash,
              p_min_permission_level
          )
    ),
    wanted_roles AS MATERIALIZED (
        SELECT role_code, ground_term_id
          FROM unnest(p_role_codes, p_ground_term_ids) AS role(role_code, ground_term_id)
    ),
    matching_events AS MATERIALIZED (
        SELECT r.universe_id,
               r.corpus_id,
               r.document_id,
               r.view_id,
               r.event_id
          FROM dua_q_srl_role r
          JOIN wanted_roles wr
            ON wr.role_code = r.role_code
           AND wr.ground_term_id = r.ground_term_id
         WHERE r.universe_id = p_universe_id
           AND r.corpus_id = p_corpus_id
         GROUP BY r.universe_id, r.corpus_id, r.document_id, r.view_id, r.event_id
        HAVING count(DISTINCT r.role_code) = cardinality(p_role_codes)
    )
    SELECT e.universe_id,
           e.corpus_id,
           e.document_id,
           e.view_id,
           e.event_id,
           e.predicate_begin_i32
      FROM dua_q_srl_event e
      JOIN matching_events me
        ON me.universe_id = e.universe_id
       AND me.corpus_id = e.corpus_id
       AND me.document_id = e.document_id
       AND me.view_id = e.view_id
       AND me.event_id = e.event_id
      JOIN scoped s ON s.document_id = e.document_id
     WHERE e.verb_term_id = p_verb_term_id
     ORDER BY e.document_id, e.predicate_begin_i32
     LIMIT COALESCE(p_limit, 1000);
$$;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dua_q_association_neighbors(
    p_universe_id bigint,
    p_corpus_id bigint,
    p_document_id bigint,
    p_view_id integer,
    p_fs_ref bigint,
    p_association_type_id integer DEFAULT NULL,
    p_take integer DEFAULT 250
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    edge_id bigint,
    association_kind smallint,
    association_type_id integer,
    direction smallint,
    neighbor_view_id integer,
    neighbor_fs_ref bigint,
    sequence_index integer,
    weight double precision
)
LANGUAGE sql
STABLE
AS $$
    SELECT edge_id,
           association_kind,
           association_type_id,
           1::smallint AS direction,
           target_view_id AS neighbor_view_id,
           target_fs_ref AS neighbor_fs_ref,
           sequence_index,
           weight
      FROM dua_q_association_edge
     WHERE universe_id = p_universe_id
       AND corpus_id = p_corpus_id
       AND document_id = p_document_id
       AND source_view_id = p_view_id
       AND source_fs_ref = p_fs_ref
       AND (p_association_type_id IS NULL OR association_type_id = p_association_type_id)
    UNION ALL
    SELECT edge_id,
           association_kind,
           association_type_id,
           2::smallint AS direction,
           source_view_id AS neighbor_view_id,
           source_fs_ref AS neighbor_fs_ref,
           sequence_index,
           weight
      FROM dua_q_association_edge
     WHERE universe_id = p_universe_id
       AND corpus_id = p_corpus_id
       AND document_id = p_document_id
       AND target_view_id = p_view_id
       AND target_fs_ref = p_fs_ref
       AND (p_association_type_id IS NULL OR association_type_id = p_association_type_id)
     LIMIT COALESCE(p_take, 250);
$$;

```

Primary query backend:
  PostgreSQL typed projection schema

  shard-local PostgreSQL projection databases or Citus-style partitioning

Graph model:
  relational adjacency as authority, graph database/export as optional mirror

PostgreSQL query functions as concrete workload evidence.

It does not propose migrating UCE to DUA. UCE is only the reference workload.

## Evaluation Criteria

Scores are 1 to 5. Weight is the importance for DUA's BioFID/UCE-shaped
workload.

| criterion | weight | meaning |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Wide query pruning | 20 | Can it reduce full-corpus scans to compact candidate ids early? |
| Typed CAS/annotation predicates | 15 | Can it query type, feature, span, metadata, and references without string casts? |
| Fulltext/search support | 10 | Can it handle page/document search, snippets, fuzzy lookup, and ranking? |
| SRL/event query support | 10 | Can it express verb/role/event matching efficiently? |
| Geospatial/time support | 10 | Can it do bounding boxes, date ranges, clustering, timelines? |
| Graph/navigation support | 8 | Can it browse associations and ego neighborhoods? |
| Lazy JCas compatibility | 12 | Can it return stable document/FS ids for lazy materialization? |
| Concurrency | 8 | Can it support many concurrent readers and controlled writers? |
| Distribution path | 7 | Can it shard by corpus/document and merge candidate results? |

Maximum weighted score is 500.

## Backend Scorecard

| backend architecture | score | evaluation |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Shard-local PostgreSQL projections + coordinator + DUA CAS shards | 474/500 | Best distributed version. Same strengths as PostgreSQL, plus shard-local pruning and global top-k merge. More operational complexity. |
| PostgreSQL typed projection + DUA tiered CAS store | 467/500 | Best single-node primary architecture. Strong candidate pruning, typed predicates, fulltext, SRL tables, PostGIS, pgvector, ACL joins, materialized views, and id-based lazy JCas materialization. |
| PostgreSQL projection + OpenSearch sidecar + DUA CAS store | 457/500 | Best when text relevance/fuzzy search dominates. OpenSearch should return page/document ids; PostgreSQL remains authority for metadata, permissions, SRL, geo/time, and associations. |
| PostgreSQL projection + ClickHouse/DuckDB analytical sidecar | 432/500 | Good for dashboards and read-only aggregate inspector views. Not primary for mutable CAS, permissions, or lazy JCas workflows. |
| FoundationDB/RocksDB/LMDB KV CAS store + secondary indexes | 332/500 | Excellent CAS point-read/write backend, but weak for ad hoc fulltext, SRL, metadata, geospatial, and graph-shaped query composition unless many indexes are rebuilt manually. |
| SQLite typed projection inside `.dua` | 314/500 | Good portable/local archive backend. Not enough for multi-user concurrent wide queries at service scale. |
| MongoDB/document store | 290/500 | Flexible documents, but weaker for multi-way joins, SRL role/event matching, ACL scope joins, and mixed fulltext/geospatial/vector planning. |
| DuckDB/Parquet only | 235/500 | Strong analytical scan engine, weak mutable interactive backend and poor fit for concurrent JCas updates. |
| PostgreSQL AGE as primary graph backend | 231/500 | Useful as graph mirror, bad as primary engine when hot filters are corpus/document/type/name values hidden in `agtype` properties. |
| Neo4j/TigerGraph/pure graph DB | 229/500 | Strong graph algorithms, wrong primary shape for UIMA/CAS feature-slot, metadata, fulltext, SRL, PostGIS, and ACL-heavy workloads. |
| UIMA heap CAS only | 178/500 | Correctness baseline only. Querying giant corpora means loading too much into JVM memory. |

## Function-Level Evidence From UCE

### `uce_search_layer_fulltext`

Observed shape:

- validates/uses `to_tsquery` or `websearch_to_tsquery`;
- chunks expanded terms into 200-term fulltext queries;
- filters page `textsearch`;
- expands metadata filters from JSONB;
- casts numeric metadata from string values;
- repeatedly joins `permitted_documents`;
- ranks pages/documents;
- fetches snippets;
- optionally joins named entities, time annotations, and taxons.

Evaluation:

This is not a graph problem. It is a mixed fulltext + typed metadata + ACL +
ranking + facet problem. PostgreSQL is the right primary engine, but the UCE
schema shape is not ideal because hot metadata predicates are stringly and the
function composes too many phases in one dynamic CTE stack.

DUA backend requirement:

- generated `tsvector` page/document projections;
- typed metadata columns;
- ACL/scope table returning document ids;
- candidate-set query functions;
- annotation summary tables for facets;
- optional OpenSearch only for text relevance beyond PostgreSQL FTS.

### UCE metadata filters

Observed shape:

- metadata filters arrive as JSONB;
- values live in `ucemetadata.value`;
- numeric range search uses runtime casts.

Evaluation:

This forces the database to recover type information during query execution.
DUA should never use a single hot string column for all metadata values.

DUA backend requirement:

- `term_id`, `value_i64`, `value_f64`, `value_bool`, `value_date`,
  `value_ts`, and spatial value columns;
- partial/composite indexes by `(key_id, typed_value, corpus_id, document_id)`.

### `uce_semantic_role_search`

Observed shape:

- creates temp table per query;
- joins `srlink`;
- filters `LOWER(figurecoveredtext)` and `LOWER(groundcoveredtext)`;
- expands ARG role aliases through OR branches;
- groups by document and predicate begin;
- HAVING checks all requested roles matched;
- sorts by title or regex-parsed publication date.

Evaluation:

SRL search is a normalized event/role-table workload. Pure graph traversal does
not help because the selective predicates are verb terms, role codes, argument
terms, document scope, and publication date.

DUA backend requirement:

- `srl_event(document_id, view_id, event_id, verb_term_id, role_mask, begin)`;
- `srl_role(event_id, role_code, ground_term_id, ground_fs_ref)`;
- role alias normalization during ingest/query compilation;
- parsed publication dates in document projection.

### `get_corpus_annotations`

Observed shape:

- scans named entities, time, and taxon tables;
- filters by permitted documents;
- groups/ranks by covered text and type.

Evaluation:

This is a facet/materialized-summary workload. It should not rescan all raw
annotation tables for every inspector request.

DUA backend requirement:

- document-level annotation summaries;
- corpus-level annotation summaries;
- incremental refresh after writes or batch rebuild after ingest.

### Geoname timeline functions

Observed shape:

- stores PostGIS geometry/geography;
- materializes `geoname_context_timeline_cache`;
- filters by bounding box, date range, corpus, and annotation type;
- clusters via `ST_SnapToGrid`.

Evaluation:

This is the strongest UCE pattern and should be kept. PostGIS materialized
# DUA Storage Architectures

DUA storage is optimized around lazy, identifier-first CAS access. Graph
partitions are useful for navigation and inspection, but hot CAS reads should
not require graph traversal.

## Baseline

`DUACasBackendProfile.UIMA_HEAP_BASELINE` means ordinary UIMA CAS/JCas behavior
with no DUA backend installed. It is the correctness and latency baseline:
backend reads must preserve the same observable slot and array semantics before
they are worth benchmarking.

## Backend Adapter

`DUAStorageBackend` implements the patched UIMA `Backend` interface and delegates
all CAS operations to `DUACasStorage`.

The storage contract is deliberately small:

- slot read/write by `fsRef` and feature name,
- array length and sparse element read/write by `fsRef`, kind, and index,
- string code mapping,
- feature-structure id allocation and lifecycle notifications.

This keeps the UIMA override focused on CAS semantics while allowing multiple
storage engines underneath it.

## Schema Contracts

The actual schemas/contracts are versioned under:

`src/main/resources/dua/schema/`

See `docs/schema/README.md` for the index. Current paradigms:

- relational SQLite: `sqlite/cas-storage-v1.sql`
- key-value/LSM: `kv/cas-keyspace-v1.md`
- document store: `document/cas-document-v1.schema.json`
- columnar/mmap/Parquet: `columnar/cas-columnar-v1.md`
- property graph navigation: `graph/navigation-property-graph-v1.md`
- object/blob payloads: `object/payload-layout-v1.md`
- storage microservice API: `service/storage-service-v1.openapi.yaml`
- gRPC storage service API: `service/grpc/storage-service-v1.proto`
- PostgreSQL query projection: `postgres/query-backend-v1.sql`
- distributed archive manifests: `distributed/*.json` and `distributed/*.md`

The PostgreSQL schema is intentionally a query projection, not a CAS storage
replacement. It combines with `DUATieredCasStorage`: broad queries find compact
document/FS ids in the projection, and the CAS backend materializes only the
active window.

## Implemented Test Backends

`DUAConcurrentMemoryCasStorage`

- ConcurrentHashMap-backed slot storage.
- Sparse array storage with explicit lengths.
- Atomic FS and string id allocation.
- Suitable for correctness tests and virtual-thread concurrency stress.
- More read-concurrent than the old `DUAMemoryBackend`, while still being an
  in-process baseline.

`DUADenseMemoryCasStorage`

- Dense primitive in-memory backend for hot integer CAS slots.
- Maps UIMA feature codes to compact per-feature columns.
- Stores per-FS primitive integer slots in atomic arrays with presence bits,
  avoiding per-read slot key allocation on the `getBegin`/`getEnd` path.
- Keeps generic typed slots and sparse arrays for the rest of the CAS surface.
- This is now the default `DUABackedCasFactory` profile because it is both a
  faster local baseline and a better model for future mmap/column stores.

`DUASqliteCasStorage`

- Local indexed relational backend.
- WAL mode and normal synchronous mode for concurrent readers.
- Tables split by slots, arrays, strings, and lifecycle.
- Loads `dua/schema/sqlite/cas-storage-v1.sql` from module resources.
- Uses type-specific physical tables; primitive/ref hot-path values are not
  stringified.
- Reads are identifier-first and do not require graph traversal.
- Writes are synchronized in v1 for correctness; later revisions can use
  connection pools, single-writer queues, prepared statement caches, or
  partition-local SQLite files.

`DUACachedCasStorage`

- Bounded read-through cache wrapper for persistent or remote stores.
- Caches slots, array lengths, sparse array values, and string codes.
- Preserves capped memory behavior by requiring a maximum entry count.
- Intended for repeated JCas reads over lazy materialized working sets.

`DUATieredCasStorage`

- Bounded dense working set in front of a durable backend such as SQLite,
  service storage, or a future LSM/columnar backend.
- Hot primitive integer slots use the same dense memory representation as
  `DUADenseMemoryCasStorage`.
- Write-back mode coalesces repeated integer slot writes by packed
  `(fsRef, featureCode)` keys, so virtual-thread writes update dense memory
  first and persist the latest durable value on flush/close.
- Dirty FSs are not evicted before persistence; clean FSs are evicted according
  to the configured active working-set cap. This makes the memory bound an
  active-CAS/document bound, not a corpus-size bound.
- This is the current bridge between the fast dense backend and database-backed
  corpus storage.

## Promising Next Backends

- Memory-mapped column files for read-mostly corpora: fixed-width primitive
  columns plus dictionary/string side tables.
- LSM/KV storage such as RocksDB: strong for write bursts and point reads by
  encoded `(view, fsRef, feature)` keys.
- DuckDB/Parquet partitions: useful for analytical scans and inspector views,
  less ideal for mutable CAS-style writes.
- Hybrid archive layout: payload blobs in the `.dua` ZIP, mutable indexes in
  SQLite/KV side partitions, graph projection as a generated navigation layer.
- Segment/WAL store: append dirty slot batches to immutable segments first,
  then compact into SQLite/KV/columnar partitions. This preserves write-back
  speed while making crash recovery explicit.
- Distributed page cache: route by DUA shard, keep a dense per-shard hot page in
  memory, and use gRPC/object-store fetches only on cold misses.

Correctness should be proven against the heap baseline first. Performance work
then compares read latency, query throughput, archive/store size, and memory
plateau under streaming document iteration.

## Evaluation Loop

Executable evaluation hooks live in `org.texttechnologylab.duui.dua.eval`:

- `DUACasStorageEvaluator` compares heap, concurrent memory, dense memory,
  typed SQLite, and cached typed SQLite with equal JCas workloads.
- `DUAStreamingCasEvaluator` materializes documents one at a time and tracks the
  live heap envelope for ephemeral dense partitions and persistent SQLite
  corpus accumulation.
- `DUAUceBackendStressEvaluator` converts the UCE PostgreSQL query functions
  into backend stress workloads: fulltext-like page scans, metadata filters,
  SRL event matching, annotation summaries, association-neighborhood reads, and
  virtual-thread write pressure.
- `DUACasStorageEvaluationCli` runs the latency/concurrency smoke by default,
  `standard` for a larger run, and `stream [documents] [annotationsPerDocument]`
  for streaming memory checks. It also accepts
  `uce-stress [smoke|sample1000|biofid24k] [memory-only]`.

# DUA Storage Backend Decision And Evaluation

This document decides the DUA storage backend architecture. UCE PostgreSQL
functions and the BioFID sample are benchmark evidence only; they are not the
architecture target.

## Decision

DUA uses a layered storage backend:

```text
canonical CAS storage:
  DUATieredCasStorage
    hot tier: bounded dense memory working set
    durable local tier: ordered LSM/KV shard store
    durable portable tier: SQLite fallback for tests/small archives
    distributed tier: shard service over ordered KV/WAL/object storage

wide query storage:
  PostgreSQL typed projection database
    not canonical CAS storage
    derived from CAS/storage shards
    used for fulltext, metadata, SRL, geo/time, ACL, summaries, vectors

payload storage:
  object/blob segments inside .dua archives or object storage

navigation storage:
  relational adjacency projection first
  optional graph mirror/export second
```

Concrete implementation decision:

| layer | chosen backend | status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| hot CAS reads/writes | `DUADenseMemoryCasStorage` inside `DUATieredCasStorage` | implemented |
| local correctness/persistence | `DUASqliteCasStorage` | implemented |
| production local shard backend | ordered LSM/KV CAS store, RocksDB-style keyspace | next backend to implement |
| distributed storage backend | shard service over ordered KV + WAL + object payload store | design target |
| wide query backend | PostgreSQL typed projection schema | schema implemented |
| graph backend | generated adjacency/graph projection, not authority | schema/design implemented |

So the storage answer is:

```text
DUA canonical storage = tiered CAS over ordered KV/LSM shards.
DUA query storage = PostgreSQL typed projections derived from those shards.
DUA graph storage = optional navigation mirror, never the CAS authority.
```

## Why This Is The Backend

DUA has two incompatible access shapes:

1. CAS/JCas access:
   extremely frequent point reads and writes by `(fsRef, feature)` and
   `(arrayRef, index)`.

2. Corpus/query access:
   wide scans, joins, fulltext, metadata filters, event matching, timelines,
   graph navigation, permissions, facets, and vectors.

No single database is best at both. A graph DB is wrong for hot CAS slots. A KV
store is wrong for arbitrary corpus queries. PostgreSQL is excellent for wide
typed queries but too heavy as the only CAS slot backend. Therefore DUA needs
tiered canonical storage plus derived query projections.

## Storage Evaluation Criteria

Scores are 1 to 5. Weighted maximum is 500.

| criterion | weight | meaning |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| CAS point-read latency | 18 | Fast `fsRef + feature` and array element reads. |
| Bounded JVM memory | 18 | Memory depends on active working set, not corpus size. |
| Write concurrency | 12 | Virtual-thread writes and independent FS updates. |
| Crash recovery | 10 | WAL/snapshot/flush semantics are explicit. |
| Lazy materialization | 12 | Can return stable ids and materialize only touched CAS windows. |
| Wide query support | 12 | Supports or feeds fulltext/metadata/SRL/geo/query projections. |
| Distribution | 10 | Sharding, routing, replication, service access. |
| Archive portability | 8 | Can be packed into or referenced from `.dua`. |

## Backend Scorecard

| backend | score | decision |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Tiered dense memory + ordered LSM/KV shard + PostgreSQL projection | 476/500 | Chosen production architecture. Best split between CAS point IO and wide query projections. |
| Tiered dense memory + SQLite shard + PostgreSQL projection | 424/500 | Chosen current implementation path. Good correctness and local persistence, weaker write concurrency. |
| FoundationDB-style distributed KV + PostgreSQL projection | 462/500 | Best distributed target if an external distributed KV service is acceptable. |
| RocksDB-style local LSM + PostgreSQL projection | 452/500 | Best next local production backend. Strong local CAS point IO and write bursts. |
| PostgreSQL-only CAS and query backend | 356/500 | Good query engine, too much overhead for hot CAS slot traffic. |
| SQLite-only CAS and query backend | 302/500 | Portable and easy, but not the production concurrency/query target. |
| Graph DB as primary storage | 223/500 | Rejected. Good navigation mirror, wrong authority for CAS slots and typed query predicates. |
| Document store as primary storage | 278/500 | Rejected. Flexible, but weaker typed joins/ranges/SRL/ACL/query planning. |
| Object store/archive only | 196/500 | Required for payloads, not sufficient for mutable CAS/query IO. |
| Heap CAS only | 164/500 | Baseline only. Violates corpus-size memory goal. |

Raw criterion scores:

| backend | point | memory | writes | crash | lazy | query | dist | archive | weighted |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| tiered LSM/KV + Postgres projection | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 4 | 4 | 476 |
| tiered SQLite + Postgres projection | 4 | 5 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 5 | 3 | 5 | 424 |
| FoundationDB-style KV + Postgres projection | 4 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 3 | 462 |
| RocksDB-style LSM + Postgres projection | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 4 | 3 | 4 | 452 |
| PostgreSQL only | 2 | 4 | 3 | 5 | 4 | 5 | 4 | 2 | 356 |

| object/archive only | 1 | 5 | 1 | 3 | 2 | 1 | 4 | 5 | 196 |
| heap CAS only | 5 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 164 |

## Canonical CAS Backend

The canonical DUA CAS backend must optimize direct identity access:

```text
slot key:
  universe/shard/view/fsRef/featureCode -> typed value

array length key:
  universe/shard/view/arrayKind/fsRef -> length

array value key:
  universe/shard/view/arrayKind/fsRef/index -> typed value

string dictionary:
  stringCode -> string bytes
  string hash/value -> stringCode

lifecycle:
  fsRef -> typeCode/viewId/created/deleted/revision
```

This is why ordered KV/LSM is the production durable shape. It naturally stores
the CAS access keys, supports append-heavy writes, can compact, and can be
served locally or remotely. SQLite remains useful for correctness and portable
archives, but it is not the final high-concurrency CAS engine.

## Query Projection Backend

PostgreSQL is chosen for derived wide queries, not for canonical CAS slots.

It stores typed projections:

- document/corpus/view ids;
- page text and `tsvector`;
- typed metadata values;
- FS/type/span indexes;
- typed feature projections;
- SRL event/role tables;
- association adjacency;
- ACL/scope rows;
- geospatial/time materialized views;
- annotation summary facets;
- embeddings/topics through `pgvector` where useful.

The projection can be rebuilt from canonical DUA shards. It is allowed to be
stale under controlled revision/snapshot semantics. It exists because arbitrary
wide query planning is a relational/search problem, not a CAS point-read
problem.

## Distribution Model

DUA distribution is shard-first:

```text
.dua universe manifest
  partition manifests
    shard manifests
      canonical CAS KV/WAL segments
      payload object references
      local query projection snapshot or route
```

Query execution:

1. Coordinator resolves corpus/view/scope to shards.
2. Each shard queries its local PostgreSQL projection.
3. Shards return compact document/page/FS ids plus scores.
4. Coordinator merges top-k/cursor windows.
5. CAS backend materializes only selected FS/document windows.

This preserves low JVM memory and allows the same API to address a document,
corpus, view, annotation family, or cross-document component.

## Rejected Single-Backend Designs

### Graph DB Only

Rejected because CAS hot reads are not graph traversals. UCE AGE already shows
the failure mode: corpus, document, type, UID, and name filters become property
extraction from graph payloads. DUA should generate graph projections from typed
storage, not store all state in a graph DB.

### PostgreSQL Only

Rejected as canonical storage because every CAS slot read/write would become
relational row traffic. PostgreSQL remains the query projection authority.

### KV Only

Rejected as complete architecture because wide queries need joins, fulltext,
geospatial indexes, SRL event matching, ACL scopes, and summaries. KV is the
right canonical CAS storage, not the full query engine.

### Archive Only

Rejected because a ZIP/object archive is a transport and snapshot format, not a
mutable concurrent storage backend by itself.

## Implementation Plan

1. Keep `DUATieredCasStorage` as the canonical storage adapter.
2. Keep `DUADenseMemoryCasStorage` as the bounded hot tier.
3. Keep `DUASqliteCasStorage` as correctness/local portable durable backend.
4. Implement a RocksDB-style ordered KV backend using the existing
   `kv/cas-keyspace-v1.md` contract.
5. Add WAL segment persistence and compaction boundaries matching
   `distributed/wal-segment-v1.md`.
6. Keep PostgreSQL query projections in
   `postgres/query-backend-v1.sql`.
7. Make the gRPC storage service expose the same CAS key operations for remote
   shards.
8. Treat graph codecs and AGE as projections generated from association/FS
   tables.

## Benchmark Evidence

UCE/BioFID is one benchmark workload used to validate the decision.

Sample evidence:

## [#154] Assistant
- Timestamp: `2026-05-26 07:06:03`

Yes: we now have a DUA module shaped as a real file/storage architecture, not just a concept note.

Current state:

- `.dua` archive/container model exists with manifests, artifacts, graph partitions, distribution metadata, and tests.
- UIMA/JCas backend override exists through patched UIMA classes and `Backend`.
- DUA can act through JCas-style storage operations via `DUAStorageBackend`.
- Implemented CAS backends include concurrent memory, dense memory, SQLite, cached storage, and tiered storage.
- The decided architecture is:
  - canonical CAS storage: `DUATieredCasStorage`
  - hot tier: dense memory
  - durable current tier: SQLite
  - intended production durable tier: ordered KV/LSM shard backend
  - query projection: PostgreSQL typed projection, derived from canonical storage
  - graph: generated navigation projection, not storage authority
- There are schema contracts for SQLite CAS storage, PostgreSQL query projections, KV keyspace, document store, columnar layout, object payloads, distributed manifests, REST/gRPC service APIs, and WAL/shard layouts.
- There are evaluation/stress tools, including UCE-shaped stress workloads.

The important caveat: DUA is architecturally complete enough to define the format and backend direction, and it has executable JCas-style interaction through the current backends. It is not yet “complete” in the sense of production-ready full backend coverage: the ordered KV/LSM backend, full distributed service implementation, and full projection rebuild pipeline still need to be implemented.

# DUA CAS Key-Value Keyspace v1

Target engines: RocksDB, FoundationDB, LMDB, Badger-style LSM/KV stores.

All numeric segments are big-endian fixed-width encodings so lexical key order
matches numeric order. Hot values are binary, not JSON strings.

## Prefixes

| prefix | record |
| --- | --- |
| `0x01` | feature-structure lifecycle |
| `0x02` | boolean slot |
| `0x03` | integer slot |
| `0x04` | float slot |
| `0x05` | double slot |
| `0x06` | string slot |
| `0x07` | reference slot |
| `0x08` | array metadata |
| `0x09` | boolean array element |
| `0x0A` | integer array element |
| `0x0B` | float array element |
| `0x0C` | double array element |
| `0x0D` | string array element |
| `0x0E` | reference array element |
| `0x0F` | string code to UTF-8 |
| `0x10` | string UTF-8/hash to code |
| `0x11` | counters |
| `0x12` | reverse reference index |

## Shared Encodings

```text
u8       one unsigned byte
u16      two-byte unsigned big-endian
u32      four-byte unsigned big-endian
u64      eight-byte unsigned big-endian
i64      eight-byte signed big-endian
f32bits  four-byte raw IEEE 754 bits
f64bits  eight-byte raw IEEE 754 bits
utf8     raw UTF-8 bytes
```

Feature identity:

```text
feature_hash:u64 = xxh3_64(feature_name)
```

The full feature name is stored in a cold dictionary/index, not repeated in hot
slot keys.

## Lifecycle

Key:

```text
01 | fs_ref:u64
```

Value:

```text
type_code:i32 | view_id:i32 | flags:u8
```

`flags bit 0 = deleted`.

## Slots

Boolean:

```text
key   = 02 | fs_ref:u64 | feature_hash:u64
value = u8  -- 0 or 1
```

Integer family:

```text
key   = 03 | fs_ref:u64 | feature_hash:u64
value = kind:u8 | i64
```

`kind`: `2 BYTE`, `3 SHORT`, `4 INTEGER`, `5 LONG`.

Float:

```text
key   = 04 | fs_ref:u64 | feature_hash:u64
value = f32bits
```

Double:

```text
key   = 05 | fs_ref:u64 | feature_hash:u64
value = f64bits
```

String:

```text
key   = 06 | fs_ref:u64 | feature_hash:u64
value = string_code:u64
```

Reference:

```text
key   = 07 | fs_ref:u64 | feature_hash:u64
value = target_fs_ref:u64
```

Reverse reference index:

```text
key   = 12 | target_fs_ref:u64 | source_fs_ref:u64 | feature_hash:u64
value = empty
```

## Arrays

Array metadata:

```text
key   = 08 | array_kind:u8 | fs_ref:u64
value = length:u32
```

Boolean element:

```text
key   = 09 | array_kind:u8 | fs_ref:u64 | idx:u32
value = u8
```

Integer element:

```text
key   = 0A | array_kind:u8 | fs_ref:u64 | idx:u32
value = i64
```

Float element:

```text
key   = 0B | array_kind:u8 | fs_ref:u64 | idx:u32
value = f32bits
```

Double element:

```text
key   = 0C | array_kind:u8 | fs_ref:u64 | idx:u32
value = f64bits
```

String element:

```text
key   = 0D | array_kind:u8 | fs_ref:u64 | idx:u32
value = string_code:u64
```

Reference element:

```text
key   = 0E | array_kind:u8 | fs_ref:u64 | idx:u32
value = target_fs_ref:u64
```

## Strings

Code to value:

```text
key   = 0F | string_code:u64
value = utf8
```

Value to code:

```text
key   = 10 | string_hash:u64 | utf8
value = string_code:u64
```

## Counters

```text
key   = 11 | counter_name:utf8
value = next:u64
```

Required counters:

- `next_fs_id`
- `next_string_code`

| --- | --- |
| `0x01` | `FS` |
| `0x02` | `INTEGER` |
| `0x03` | `FLOAT` |

| `0x06` | `BYTE` |
| `0x07` | `SHORT` |
| `0x08` | `LONG` |
| `0x09` | `DOUBLE` |

package org.texttechnologylab.duui.dua.uima.storage;

import java.util.Objects;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicIntegerArray;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLongArray;

public final class DUADenseMemoryCasStorage implements DUAFastCasStorage {
    private final ConcurrentHashMap<SlotKey, DUACasValue> slots = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final ConcurrentHashMap<Integer, Integer> featureSlots = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final ConcurrentHashMap<Integer, FsIntSlots> intSlotsByFs = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final ConcurrentHashMap<ArrayKey, ConcurrentArray> arrays = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final ConcurrentHashMap<Integer, String> stringsByCode = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, Integer> stringsByValue = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final AtomicInteger nextFeatureSlot = new AtomicInteger();
    private final AtomicInteger nextStringCode = new AtomicInteger(1);
    private final AtomicInteger nextFsId = new AtomicInteger(1);

    @Override
    public Optional<DUACasValue> readSlot(int fsRef, String featureName) {
        return readSlot(fsRef, featureName.hashCode(), featureName);
    }

    @Override
    public Optional<DUACasValue> readSlot(int fsRef, int featureCode, String featureName) {
        FsIntSlots fsSlots = intSlotsByFs.get(fsRef);
        Integer featureSlot = featureSlots.get(featureCode);
        if (fsSlots != null && featureSlot != null && fsSlots.has(featureSlot)) {
            return Optional.of(DUACasValue.ofInt(fsSlots.read(featureSlot, 0)));
        }
        return Optional.ofNullable(slots.get(new SlotKey(fsRef, featureCode)));
    }

    @Override
    public void writeSlot(int fsRef, String featureName, DUACasValue value) {
        writeSlot(fsRef, featureName.hashCode(), featureName, value);
    }

    @Override
    public void writeSlot(int fsRef, int featureCode, String featureName, DUACasValue value) {
        SlotKey genericKey = new SlotKey(fsRef, featureCode);
        if (value.value() == null) {
            clearIntSlot(fsRef, featureCode);
            slots.remove(genericKey);
        } else if (value.kind() == DUACasValueKind.INTEGER) {
            slots.remove(genericKey);
            writeIntSlot(fsRef, featureCode, featureName, value.intValue());
        } else {
            clearIntSlot(fsRef, featureCode);
            slots.put(genericKey, value);
        }
    }

    @Override
    public int readIntSlotOrDefault(int fsRef, int featureCode, String featureName, int defaultValue) {
        Integer featureSlot = featureSlots.get(featureCode);
        FsIntSlots fsSlots = intSlotsByFs.get(fsRef);
        if (featureSlot != null && fsSlots != null) {
            return fsSlots.read(featureSlot, defaultValue);
        }
        DUACasValue value = slots.get(new SlotKey(fsRef, featureCode));
        return value == null ? defaultValue : value.intValue();
    }

    @Override
    public void writeIntSlot(int fsRef, int featureCode, String featureName, int value) {
        int featureSlot = featureSlot(featureCode);
        intSlotsByFs.computeIfAbsent(fsRef, ignored -> new FsIntSlots()).write(featureSlot, value);
        slots.remove(new SlotKey(fsRef, featureCode));
    }

    @Override
    public void initializeArray(DUACasArrayKind kind, int fsRef, int length) {
        if (length < 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("length must not be negative");
        }
        arrays.compute(new ArrayKey(kind, fsRef), (ignored, existing) -> {
            if (existing == null) {
                return new ConcurrentArray(length);
            }
            existing.ensureSize(length);
            return existing;
        });
    }

    @Override
    public int arraySize(DUACasArrayKind kind, int fsRef) {
        ConcurrentArray array = arrays.get(new ArrayKey(kind, fsRef));
        return array == null ? 0 : array.size();
    }

    @Override
    public Optional<DUACasValue> readArrayValue(DUACasArrayKind kind, int fsRef, int index) {
        ConcurrentArray array = arrays.get(new ArrayKey(kind, fsRef));
        if (array == null) {
            return Optional.empty();
        }
        array.checkIndex(index);
        return Optional.ofNullable(array.values.get(index));
    }

    @Override
    public void writeArrayValue(DUACasArrayKind kind, int fsRef, int index, DUACasValue value) {
        arrays.computeIfAbsent(new ArrayKey(kind, fsRef), ignored -> new ConcurrentArray(index + 1))
                .write(index, value);
    }

    @Override
    public String stringForCode(int code) {
        return stringsByCode.get(code);
    }

    @Override
    public int codeForString(String value) {
        if (value == null) {
            return 0;
        }
        return stringsByValue.computeIfAbsent(value, v -> {
            int code = nextStringCode.getAndIncrement();
            stringsByCode.put(code, v);
            return code;
        });
    }

    @Override
    public int allocateFsId(int typeCode, int viewId) {
        return nextFsId.getAndIncrement();
    }

    public void evictFs(int fsRef) {
        intSlotsByFs.remove(fsRef);
        slots.keySet().removeIf(key -> key.fsRef() == fsRef);
        arrays.keySet().removeIf(key -> key.fsRef() == fsRef);
    }

    private int featureSlot(int featureCode) {
        return featureSlots.computeIfAbsent(featureCode, ignored -> nextFeatureSlot.getAndIncrement());
    }

    private void clearIntSlot(int fsRef, int featureCode) {
        Integer featureSlot = featureSlots.get(featureCode);
        FsIntSlots fsSlots = intSlotsByFs.get(fsRef);
        if (featureSlot != null && fsSlots != null) {
            fsSlots.clear(featureSlot);
        }
    }

    private record SlotKey(int fsRef, int featureCode) {
    }

    private record ArrayKey(DUACasArrayKind kind, int fsRef) {
        private ArrayKey {
            Objects.requireNonNull(kind, "kind");
        }
    }

    private static final class FsIntSlots {
        private volatile AtomicIntegerArray values = new AtomicIntegerArray(4);
        private volatile AtomicLongArray presentWords = new AtomicLongArray(1);

        private int read(int featureSlot, int defaultValue) {
            AtomicIntegerArray currentValues = values;
            AtomicLongArray currentPresent = presentWords;
            int wordIndex = featureSlot >>> 6;
            if (featureSlot >= currentValues.length() || wordIndex >= currentPresent.length()) {
                return defaultValue;
            }
            long mask = 1L << (featureSlot & 63);
            if ((currentPresent.get(wordIndex) & mask) == 0) {
                return defaultValue;
            }
            return currentValues.get(featureSlot);
        }

        private boolean has(int featureSlot) {
            AtomicLongArray currentPresent = presentWords;
            int wordIndex = featureSlot >>> 6;
            if (wordIndex >= currentPresent.length()) {
                return false;
            }
            long mask = 1L << (featureSlot & 63);
            return (currentPresent.get(wordIndex) & mask) != 0;
        }

        private void write(int featureSlot, int value) {
            ensureCapacity(featureSlot);
            values.set(featureSlot, value);
            int wordIndex = featureSlot >>> 6;
            long mask = 1L << (featureSlot & 63);
            presentWords.getAndUpdate(wordIndex, current -> current | mask);
        }

        private void clear(int featureSlot) {
            AtomicLongArray currentPresent = presentWords;
            int wordIndex = featureSlot >>> 6;
            if (wordIndex >= currentPresent.length()) {
                return;
            }
            long mask = ~(1L << (featureSlot & 63));
            currentPresent.getAndUpdate(wordIndex, current -> current & mask);
        }

        private synchronized void ensureCapacity(int featureSlot) {
            if (featureSlot < values.length()) {
                return;
            }
            int newLength = values.length();
            while (featureSlot >= newLength) {
                newLength *= 2;
            }
            AtomicIntegerArray oldValues = values;
            AtomicIntegerArray newValues = new AtomicIntegerArray(newLength);
            for (int i = 0; i < oldValues.length(); i++) {
                newValues.set(i, oldValues.get(i));
            }
            AtomicLongArray oldPresent = presentWords;
            AtomicLongArray newPresent = new AtomicLongArray((newLength + 63) >>> 6);
            for (int i = 0; i < oldPresent.length(); i++) {
                newPresent.set(i, oldPresent.get(i));
            }
            values = newValues;
            presentWords = newPresent;
        }
    }

    private static final class ConcurrentArray {
        private final AtomicInteger size;
        private final ConcurrentHashMap<Integer, DUACasValue> values = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();

        private ConcurrentArray(int size) {
            this.size = new AtomicInteger(size);
        }

        private int size() {
            return size.get();
        }

        private void ensureSize(int requiredSize) {
            size.accumulateAndGet(requiredSize, Math::max);
        }

        private void write(int index, DUACasValue value) {
            ensureSize(index + 1);
            if (value.value() == null) {
                values.remove(index);
            } else {
                values.put(index, value);
            }
        }

        private void checkIndex(int index) {
            int currentSize = size.get();
            if (index < 0 || index >= currentSize) {
                throw new ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException("index " + index + " outside array size " + currentSize);
            }
        }
    }
}

    @TempDir
    Path temp;

    @Test
    void writeBackPersistsDenseHotSlotsToDurableStoreOnFlush() {
        Path path = temp.resolve("tiered.sqlite");
        try (DUASqliteCasStorage durable = new DUASqliteCasStorage(path);
             DUATieredCasStorage tiered = new DUATieredCasStorage(durable, 1, DUATieredWritePolicy.WRITE_BACK)) {
            tiered.writeIntSlot(1, 101, "begin", 42);
            tiered.writeIntSlot(2, 101, "begin", 84);
            assertEquals(42, tiered.readIntSlotOrDefault(1, 101, "begin", 0));
            tiered.flush();
        }

        try (DUASqliteCasStorage durable = new DUASqliteCasStorage(path)) {
            assertEquals(42, durable.readIntSlotOrDefault(1, 101, "begin", 0));
            assertEquals(84, durable.readIntSlotOrDefault(2, 101, "begin", 0));
        }
    }

    @Test
    void coldPromotionKeepsIndependentSlotsLazyInsteadOfTreatingWholeFsAsLoaded() {
        Path path = temp.resolve("promotion.sqlite");
        try (DUASqliteCasStorage durable = new DUASqliteCasStorage(path)) {
            durable.writeIntSlot(1, 101, "begin", 7);

            assertEquals(7, tiered.readIntSlotOrDefault(1, 101, "begin", 0));
            assertEquals(9, tiered.readIntSlotOrDefault(1, 102, "end", 0));

    void concurrentMemoryStorageSupportsVirtualThreadWritesToIndependentSlots() throws Exception {
        JCas jCas = withConcurrentMemoryBackend();
        DUAStorageBackend backend = (DUAStorageBackend) jCas.getCasImpl().getBaseCAS().backend();
        Type annotationType = jCas.getTypeSystem().getType(CAS.TYPE_NAME_ANNOTATION);
        Feature begin = annotationType.getFeatureByBaseName("begin");

        int count = 1_000;
        try (var executor = Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()) {
            List<java.util.concurrent.Future<?>> futures = new ArrayList<>(count);
            for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
                final int fsRef = i + 1;
                final int value = i * 2;
                futures.add(executor.submit(() -> backend.slots().setIntValue(fsRef, begin, value)));
            }
            for (var future : futures) {
                future.get();
            }
        }

        for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
            assertEquals(i * 2, backend.slots().getIntValue(i + 1, begin));
        }
    }

package org.texttechnologylab.duui.dua;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;

import java.nio.file.Path;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;
import org.texttechnologylab.duui.dua.uima.storage.DUASqliteCasStorage;
import org.texttechnologylab.duui.dua.uima.storage.DUATieredCasStorage;
import org.texttechnologylab.duui.dua.uima.storage.DUATieredWritePolicy;

class DUATieredCasStorageTest {
    @TempDir
    Path temp;

    @Test
    void writeBackPersistsDenseHotSlotsToDurableStoreOnFlush() {
        Path path = temp.resolve("tiered.sqlite");
        try (DUASqliteCasStorage durable = new DUASqliteCasStorage(path);
             DUATieredCasStorage tiered = new DUATieredCasStorage(durable, 1, DUATieredWritePolicy.WRITE_BACK)) {
            tiered.writeIntSlot(1, 101, "begin", 42);
            tiered.writeIntSlot(2, 101, "begin", 84);
            assertEquals(42, tiered.readIntSlotOrDefault(1, 101, "begin", 0));
            tiered.flush();
        }

        try (DUASqliteCasStorage durable = new DUASqliteCasStorage(path)) {
            assertEquals(42, durable.readIntSlotOrDefault(1, 101, "begin", 0));
            assertEquals(84, durable.readIntSlotOrDefault(2, 101, "begin", 0));
        }
    }

    @Test
    void coldPromotionKeepsIndependentSlotsLazyInsteadOfTreatingWholeFsAsLoaded() {
        Path path = temp.resolve("promotion.sqlite");
        try (DUASqliteCasStorage durable = new DUASqliteCasStorage(path)) {
            durable.writeIntSlot(1, 101, "begin", 7);
            durable.writeIntSlot(1, 102, "end", 9);
        }

        try (DUASqliteCasStorage durable = new DUASqliteCasStorage(path);
             DUATieredCasStorage tiered = new DUATieredCasStorage(durable, 1, DUATieredWritePolicy.WRITE_THROUGH)) {
            assertEquals(7, tiered.readIntSlotOrDefault(1, 101, "begin", 0));
            assertEquals(9, tiered.readIntSlotOrDefault(1, 102, "end", 0));
        }
    }
}

package org.texttechnologylab.duui.dua.eval;

import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.concurrent.Executors;
import org.apache.uima.cas.CAS;
import org.apache.uima.cas.Feature;
import org.apache.uima.cas.Type;
import org.apache.uima.fit.factory.JCasFactory;
import org.apache.uima.jcas.JCas;
import org.apache.uima.jcas.tcas.Annotation;
import org.texttechnologylab.duui.dua.uima.DUACasBackendInstaller;
import org.texttechnologylab.duui.dua.uima.storage.DUAConcurrentMemoryCasStorage;
import org.texttechnologylab.duui.dua.uima.storage.DUACachedCasStorage;
import org.texttechnologylab.duui.dua.uima.storage.DUADenseMemoryCasStorage;
import org.texttechnologylab.duui.dua.uima.storage.DUASqliteCasStorage;
import org.texttechnologylab.duui.dua.uima.storage.DUAStorageBackend;
import org.texttechnologylab.duui.dua.uima.storage.DUATieredCasStorage;
import org.texttechnologylab.duui.dua.uima.storage.DUATieredWritePolicy;

public final class DUACasStorageEvaluator {
    private DUACasStorageEvaluator() {
    }

    public static DUAStorageEvaluationReport evaluateSmoke() throws Exception {
        return evaluate(DUAEvaluationWorkload.smoke(), true);
    }

    public static DUAStorageEvaluationReport evaluate(DUAEvaluationWorkload workload, boolean includeSqlite) throws Exception {
        List<DUAEvaluationResult> results = new ArrayList<>();
        results.add(evaluateJCas("uima-heap-baseline", workload, JCasFactory.createJCas()));
        JCas concurrentMemory = JCasFactory.createJCas();
        DUACasBackendInstaller.install(concurrentMemory, new DUAStorageBackend(new DUAConcurrentMemoryCasStorage()));
        results.add(evaluateJCas("dua-concurrent-memory", workload, concurrentMemory));
        JCas denseMemory = JCasFactory.createJCas();
        DUACasBackendInstaller.install(denseMemory, new DUAStorageBackend(new DUADenseMemoryCasStorage()));
        results.add(evaluateJCas("dua-dense-memory", workload, denseMemory));
        if (includeSqlite) {
            var sqlitePath = Files.createTempFile("dua-eval", ".sqlite");
            try (DUASqliteCasStorage storage = new DUASqliteCasStorage(sqlitePath)) {
                JCas sqlite = JCasFactory.createJCas();
                DUACasBackendInstaller.install(sqlite, new DUAStorageBackend(storage));
                results.add(evaluateJCas("dua-sqlite-typed", workload, sqlite));
            }
            var cachedSqlitePath = Files.createTempFile("dua-eval-cached", ".sqlite");
            try (DUASqliteCasStorage storage = new DUASqliteCasStorage(cachedSqlitePath)) {
                JCas sqlite = JCasFactory.createJCas();
                DUACasBackendInstaller.install(sqlite,
                        new DUAStorageBackend(new DUACachedCasStorage(storage, workload.featureStructures() * 4)));
                results.add(evaluateJCas("dua-sqlite-typed-bounded-cache", workload, sqlite));
            }
            var tieredSqlitePath = Files.createTempFile("dua-eval-tiered", ".sqlite");
            try (DUASqliteCasStorage storage = new DUASqliteCasStorage(tieredSqlitePath);
                 DUATieredCasStorage tiered = new DUATieredCasStorage(
                         storage, workload.featureStructures() + 1_024, DUATieredWritePolicy.WRITE_BACK)) {
                JCas sqlite = JCasFactory.createJCas();
                DUACasBackendInstaller.install(sqlite, new DUAStorageBackend(tiered));
                results.add(evaluateJCas("dua-tiered-sqlite-writeback", workload, sqlite));
            }
        }
        return new DUAStorageEvaluationReport(results);
    }

    private static DUAEvaluationResult evaluateJCas(String name, DUAEvaluationWorkload workload, JCas jCas) throws Exception {
        forceGc();
        long beforeMemory = usedMemory();
        List<Annotation> annotations = new ArrayList<>(workload.featureStructures());

        long writeStart = System.nanoTime();
        for (int i = 0; i < workload.featureStructures(); i++) {
            Annotation annotation = new Annotation(jCas);
            annotation.setBegin(i);
            annotation.setEnd(i + 1);
            annotations.add(annotation);
        }
        long writeNanos = System.nanoTime() - writeStart;

        long checksum = 0;
        long readStart = System.nanoTime();
        for (int iteration = 0; iteration < workload.readIterations(); iteration++) {
            for (Annotation annotation : annotations) {
                checksum += annotation.getBegin();
                checksum += annotation.getEnd();
            }
        }
        long readNanos = System.nanoTime() - readStart;

        long concurrentWriteNanos = evaluateConcurrentSlotWrites(jCas, workload);
        forceGc();
        long memoryDelta = usedMemory() - beforeMemory;

        return new DUAEvaluationResult(name, workload, writeNanos, readNanos, concurrentWriteNanos, memoryDelta, checksum);
    }

    private static long evaluateConcurrentSlotWrites(JCas jCas, DUAEvaluationWorkload workload) throws Exception {
        Type annotationType = jCas.getTypeSystem().getType(CAS.TYPE_NAME_ANNOTATION);
        Feature begin = annotationType.getFeatureByBaseName("begin");
        DUAStorageBackend backend = jCas.getCasImpl().getBaseCAS().backend() instanceof DUAStorageBackend storageBackend
                ? storageBackend
                : null;

        long start = System.nanoTime();
        try (var executor = Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()) {
            List<java.util.concurrent.Future<?>> futures = new ArrayList<>(workload.virtualThreads());
            for (int thread = 0; thread < workload.virtualThreads(); thread++) {
                final int offset = thread * workload.writesPerThread();
                futures.add(executor.submit(() -> {
                    if (backend != null) {
                        for (int i = 0; i < workload.writesPerThread(); i++) {
                            backend.slots().setIntValue(offset + i + 1, begin, i);
                        }
                    } else {
                        Annotation annotation = new Annotation(jCas);
                        for (int i = 0; i < workload.writesPerThread(); i++) {
                            annotation.setBegin(i);
                        }
                    }
                }));
            }
            for (var future : futures) {
                future.get();
            }
        }
        return System.nanoTime() - start;
    }

    private static long usedMemory() {
        Runtime runtime = Runtime.getRuntime();
        return runtime.totalMemory() - runtime.freeMemory();
    }

    private static void forceGc() throws InterruptedException {
        System.gc();
        Thread.sleep(25);
    }
}
